In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the unmodified t tests are valid under Gaussianity and constant population mean assumption if and only if the variance–covariances of the observation vectors are circularly structured.

the circularity condition, which has been shown to be sufficient for valid unmodified correlation analysis with autocovariance–covariance matrices of arbitrary rank, can be considered as a natural and effective substitute for the sphericity (or compound symmetry) condition, which is only sufficient in the special case where the observation vectors are uncorrelated (or possess a compound symmetry structure) and possess the same variance structure up to a positive constant.

the circularity condition for valid correlation testing is the natural generalization of the sphericity requirement for valid ANOVA testing.

the circularity condition (i.e., circularity in the variance–covariace matrix of one of two observation vectors, or in both) is the weakest sufficient condition for valid t testing in correlation and repeated measures analysis.
the unmodified t tests are not valid when the data are not circular.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when the circularity condition holds for one of the observation vectors, unmodified t testing is valid for correlation analysis with autocorreleated and heteroscedastc sample data.
the circularity condition should be preferred over the sphericity one, when the unmodified t testing is used for correlation analysis with autocorreleted and heteroscedastictic sample data.

the circularity condition for valid unmodiﬁed t testing in correlation and repeated measures analysis can be viewed as a natural generalization of the sphericity requirement for the unmodified F test in the repeated measures analysis of variance.
